chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad altogether, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who visited the House before shaving [his head]. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he visited the House before shaving, and he knew that this was not befitting for him, then upon him is the blood of a sheep [as expiation].'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim who visits the Kaaba before shaving his head?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who performs Ziyarah before Halq, emphasizing that the penalty of Damm (sacrificing a sheep) applies specifically when the deviation is done knowingly and intentionally. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the distinction between mere sequence errors and deliberate disregard for the prescribed ritual order, linking the act to the broader concept of compensating for ritual imperfections. The ruling underscores the importance of mindfulness (Tadabbur) in fulfilling the pillars of Hajj as taught by Imam al-Sadiq (AS).
